субота.text:
From Old East Slavic субота (subota), from Byzantine Greek *σάμβατον (*sámbaton), from Ancient Greek σάββατα (sábbata), from Aramaic שַׁבְּתָא (šabbǝtā) or Hebrew שַׁבָּת (šabbāṯ). Cognates include Russian суббо́та (subbóta), Belarusian субо́та (subóta), Old Church Slavonic сѫбота (sǫbota), Bulgarian съ́бота (sắbota), Serbo-Croatian су́бота.
Compare with Old Church Slavonic собота (sobota) (Czech sobota, Slovak sobota, Polabian sobota, Polish sobota, Silesian sobota, Lower Sorbian sobota, Upper Sorbian sobota, Slovene sobota) which is from Medieval Latin sabbatum (cf. sabbata (“the seventh day, Sabbath”) http://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.04.0060%3Aentry%3Dsabbata), from Ancient Greek σάββατα (sábbata) (freq. in pl. of the single).
